title: LLM cost, metering, keys and caching

questions.text: Through which single client does this paid call go, and does it emit one raw-unit usage event per attempt?
What is the worst-case cost of one trigger with the largest allowed input? Show the arithmetic.
What stops it: per-job ceiling, per-tenant quota, kill switch? What does each do on error? (It must deny.)
Who pays (BYOK, gateway or system key), and how will I see that from the response, not from config?
Which model, and which eval shows a cheaper one is not good enough? Can it run batched?
What event triggers the call, and what predicate skips it? Have we computed this result before (cache key, TTL, negative cache)?
Is the prompt prefix stable and over the model's minimum cacheable length? Where is the breakpoint, and what changes before it?
Where do limits come from at decision time (source of truth or a cache), and how stale can they be?
For experiments: sample size from a power analysis, cost estimate, budget, stop rule. For keys: ledger state checked before testing?

For each cached call: where is each breakpoint, and what in it or before it changes per call or per task (time, ids, place, ranked or retrieved text, the tool list)? Does the varying part sit after the breakpoint as its own block or message? Is it request-level (automatic) cache_control, and is the last block unique per call?

Who reads this prefix back, and how soon: calls sharing it within the TTL (measured gaps), its size against the model's minimum cacheable length, the TTL chosen (5 min or 1 h), and does metering record 1-hour writes as their own unit?

If the loop compacts, clears or windows its history: how many steps per 100 rewrite the cached prefix, does it clear in large chunks (hysteresis: trigger high, clear at least N tokens), and do all windows and limits step on the same turns?

Does anyone wait for this result within minutes? If not (nightly or cron job, backfill, re-index, eval run, bulk extraction), why is it not on a batch API (Anthropic Message Batches: -50%, most batches done within 1 h, expired after 24 h, up to 100,000 requests or 256 MB per batch)? If steps chain, how many rounds, and what is the wall time at up to 24 h each?

Which request parameters can change between calls of one conversation or job: tool definitions or their order, tool_choice, disable_parallel_tool_use, images present or absent, thinking mode or budget, effort, web search or citations toggles? Each one invalidates the cache from its level on (tools -> system -> messages).

For the TTL chosen, show the break-even with measured reuse gaps: a 5-minute write pays over no cache when reads per written token > 0.28, a 1-hour write when > 1.11; 1-hour beats 5-minute once at least one reuse per hour lands after the 5-minute window.

Do parallel calls share a cached prefix? Is the first response awaited before the rest go out (a cache entry is readable only after the first response starts)? For a batch with a shared prefix, is the prefix written first with a 1-hour TTL?

budgets.measure: worst-case arithmetic in pre-flight + metered sum per job
bypass scan (cost.direct-sdk) outside the metered client
budgets.source: design by contract: single choke point

budgets.measure: metered sum vs provider usage export per provider per day
cache_read / (uncached + cache_read + cache_write) per hot call site (agent loop, chat, repeated batch) over 7 days, from usage records (cache-probe.mjs usage)
budgets.source: judgement threshold: loops that read new tool output write it once on any layout; tune from a measured baseline

budgets.measure: cache_read tokens / cache_write tokens per call site; under break-even the cache costs more than no cache (0.28 for 5-minute writes, 1.11 for 1-hour writes)
budgets.source: Anthropic prompt caching pricing: write 1.25x (5 min) or 2x (1 h), read 0.1x base input

budgets.measure: loop steps whose cache_write exceeds the step's new content, per 100 steps, in a replay of real long turns
budgets.source: Anthropic context editing: clearing invalidates the cached prefix; clear_at_least makes each invalidation worth it

budgets.measure: share of model spend from call sites nobody waits on (cron, backfill, eval, bulk) sent as synchronous calls, from usage records grouped by site
budgets.source: Anthropic Message Batches: 50% of standard price for work that does not need an immediate response (the share is a judgement threshold)

budgets.measure: per cached prefix: reuses per hour that land 5-60 min after the previous use (cache-probe.mjs usage gaps). For k such reuses 1-hour costs 2 + 0.1k and 5-minute 1.25(k+1) base-input units: 1-hour is cheaper from k = 1 (k > 0.65)
budgets.source: Anthropic prompt caching pricing: write 1.25x (5 min) or 2x (1 h), read 0.1x

rules.title: Provider SDK used directly outside the metered client
rules.why: Every call here is spend nobody records or bills.
rules.confirm: failing-test: mock the provider, call the path, assert one usage event per attempt (fails: zero)
rules.fixHint: route through the project's metered client; set metered paths in .jstack/unslop.json extraRules if they differ

rules.title: Quota/spend gate that allows on error (catch returns true/null)
rules.why: When the quota store is down, every paid call goes through (CWE-636).
rules.confirm: failing-test: make the quota store throw; assert the paid call is not made
rules.fixHint: deny on error for paid actions; document any degrade mode

rules.title: Gate defaults to allow (?? true / || true)
rules.why: A missing limit reads as unlimited.
rules.confirm: failing-test: limit row absent; assert denied

rules.title: Per-item paid call in a loop with no size bound or job ceiling before it
rules.why: A big upload (or a zip bomb) multiplies the bill.
rules.confirm: failing-test: 10k-entry archive through the entry point with the provider mocked; calls before rejection > N

rules.title: Message or webhook handler calls the model on every event
rules.why: Group chatter becomes paid calls.
rules.confirm: failing-test: replay a chat log; paid calls > messages meeting the trigger

rules.title: Per-call or per-task content (time, ids, place, user name, ranked or retrieved text) in or before the cached prefix; tools in non-deterministic order
rules.why: Every request misses the prompt cache.
rules.confirm: measurement: cache-probe.mjs replay of two calls for different tasks or users: verdict write-only or prefix-moved; prompt prefix diff up to the breakpoint
rules.fixHint: split the prompt: the stable part under the breakpoint, the varying part after it as its own block or message

rules.title: Usage logged as converted credits or dollars instead of raw provider units
rules.why: Pricing changes cannot be replayed; reconciliation with the invoice breaks.
rules.confirm: static-proof: the usage event has no input/output token fields

rules.title: One spend or rate pool shared by several agents or users with no per-consumer cap
rules.why: One busy consumer spends the pool and every other one is refused.
rules.confirm: failing-test: consumer A loops until the pool is spent; consumer B is refused

rules.title: Quota or plan limit read from the session, token claims or a long-lived cache at decision time
rules.why: A raised or lowered limit takes effect only after re-login, so users are blocked or overspend.
rules.confirm: failing-test: raise the limit in the store; the next request is still refused until re-login

rules.title: Request-level (automatic) cache_control on a Messages call
rules.why: Automatic caching puts the breakpoint on the last block. When that block is unique per call, every call writes the whole prompt at 1.25x or 2x and nothing reads it: more than no cache.
rules.confirm: measurement: cache-probe.mjs replay of the same request twice; verdict write-only (second call cache_read 0, cache_write > 0)
rules.fixHint: block-level breakpoints on what repeats (tools, system, a stable first turn), the per-call part after them unmarked; keep automatic caching only for multi-turn conversations whose last block the next turn reads

rules.title: Clock, random value or uuid interpolated into a system prompt
rules.why: The system prompt renders before the messages, so a value that changes per call breaks the cached prefix of everything after it: every call writes again.
rules.confirm: measurement: cache-probe.mjs replay of two calls a minute apart; verdict write-only or prefix-moved
rules.fixHint: keep the system prompt stable under the breakpoint; send the time, ids or place after it as their own block or in the user turn

rules.title: Tool list built from a set (order not stable across processes)
rules.why: Tools render first in the cached prefix; string-hash randomisation reorders a set per process, so each worker or restart rewrites the whole cache.
rules.confirm: repro-script: build the tool list in two processes with different PYTHONHASHSEED; the serialised lists differ
rules.fixHint: sort the tools by name (or keep a fixed list) before sending

rules.title: Breakpoint on content that is unique per call (the last block, a per-call turn, a retry note)
rules.why: Each call writes its whole prompt at the write premium and no later call reads it.
rules.confirm: measurement: cache-probe.mjs replay of the same request twice, or cache-probe.mjs usage on the site: reads per write under break-even

rules.title: History compaction or tool-result clearing that removes a little on almost every step
rules.why: Every clear rewrites the cached prefix from the cut, so a loop past its threshold pays a cache write per step.
rules.confirm: measurement: replay a long real turn through the compactor: rewrites per 100 steps over cost.cache_rewrites_per_100_steps; or usage records: cache_write per step far above the step's new content
rules.fixHint: hysteresis: trigger high and clear down to a much lower target (clear at least N tokens), so clears are rare and each is worth its write

rules.title: Two history windows or limits that step on different turns
rules.why: Each step of either window changes earlier history, so the prefix is rewritten on alternate turns instead of once per cycle.
rules.confirm: measurement: deterministic replay of stored conversations: share of turns where an earlier message changed
rules.fixHint: derive every window from one step counter so they move on the same turns

rules.title: Cache breakpoint on single-call work (one call per document, hours apart)
rules.why: Nothing reads the prefix back within the TTL, so the breakpoint only adds the write premium.
rules.confirm: measurement: cache-probe.mjs usage on the site: cache_read 0 or reads per write under break-even, gaps over the TTL

rules.title: Cached prefix shorter than the model's minimum cacheable length
rules.why: Below the minimum the request is processed without caching and no error is returned: the breakpoint does nothing.
rules.confirm: measurement: token count of the prefix vs the model's documented minimum; usage shows cache_write 0 and cache_read 0 (cache-probe.mjs verdict not-cached)

rules.title: Cache TTL chosen without measured reuse gaps, or 1-hour writes metered at the 5-minute rate
rules.why: A 1-hour write costs 2x input against 1.25x: it pays only when enough reads land 5-60 min later, and metering that folds it into 5-minute writes under-bills.
rules.confirm: measurement: cache-probe.mjs usage gaps_over_ttl_pct and reads per write vs break-even per TTL; static-proof: the usage event has no separate 1-hour write field

rules.title: Hot path (agent or chat loop) on a provider or model that reports ~0 cache reads
rules.why: A loop resends its growing history every step; with no cache each step pays full input on all of it.
rules.confirm: measurement: cache-probe.mjs usage on the site over a day: hit_pct near 0 with more than one call per session

rules.title: Cache-invalidating request parameter chosen per call (tool_choice, thinking, budget_tokens, effort, disable_parallel_tool_use set by a conditional)
rules.why: tool_choice, disable_parallel_tool_use and the thinking configuration (mode, budget, effort) are rendered into the prompt: a change invalidates the messages cache, and on some models the tools and system caches too. A value that flips between calls of one conversation rewrites its history on each flip.
rules.confirm: measurement: cache-probe.mjs replay of two consecutive calls of one conversation where the value differs; verdict prefix-moved or write-only
rules.fixHint: keep the value fixed for the conversation; when it must vary, put a breakpoint before the variation point

rules.title: Synchronous model call in a cron, nightly, backfill or eval job with no batch API in the file
rules.why: Nobody waits on a scheduled or bulk job, yet each synchronous call pays the full price: the same requests on a batch API cost half.
rules.confirm: static-proof: the job's trigger is a schedule or a bulk run and no caller waits on the result (read the scheduler entry); the saving is the site's metered spend x 0.5
rules.fixHint: submit the items as one batch (custom_id per item, poll or webhook for the end, handle errored and expired results); keep synchronous calls only for steps a person waits on

rules.title: Clock interpolated into a content block that carries the cache breakpoint
rules.why: The breakpoint sits on a block whose text changes every call, so each call writes a new entry at the write premium and none is ever read.
rules.confirm: measurement: cache-probe.mjs replay of the same request a minute apart; verdict write-only
rules.fixHint: move the time out of the marked block: the stable text keeps the breakpoint, the time goes after it (its own block or the user turn), at the granularity the task needs (the day, not the millisecond)

rules.title: Parallel calls that share a cached prefix sent at once, with nothing written yet
rules.why: A cache entry is readable only after the first response starts, so N parallel calls each write the prefix: N writes, no reads.
rules.confirm: measurement: usage records of one fan-out: cache_creation > 0 on more than one call of the same prefix within a second

rules.title: Batch of requests sharing a long prefix with no breakpoint, or a 5-minute TTL on it
rules.why: Batch requests run concurrently and in any order, and a batch often takes 5-60 min: a 5-minute entry expires between requests, so most of them pay the prefix in full.
rules.confirm: measurement: cache-probe.mjs usage over the batch results: hit_pct low with a prefix over the minimum cacheable length

rules.title: Batch API used where a person waits for the result or where steps chain
rules.why: A batch can take up to 24 h and returns results only when every request has ended; a waiting user or a five-step chain turns half price into hours of wall time.
rules.confirm: measurement: end-to-end wall time of the flow on a real batch vs the latency budget of its caller

rules.title: Conversation breakpoint fixed on an early turn, or turns that add 20+ blocks with one breakpoint
rules.why: Each new turn pays its whole history after the fixed breakpoint; when a turn pushes the breakpoint 20 or more blocks past the last write, the lookback misses it and the whole history is written again.
rules.confirm: measurement: cache-probe.mjs usage on a long conversation: uncached input grows turn by turn, or a full rewrite after a tool-heavy turn

rules.title: Error while collecting a batch's results discards the items already received and re-runs the whole set
rules.why: Answered items were billed and metered already; the fallback pays for them again.
rules.confirm: failing-test: fail result collection at item k of n; only n-k items may be re-run
rules.fixHint: persist each result as it streams and retry only the missing ones

verify.text: bypass scan clean (scan.mjs cost.direct-sdk / ESLint no-restricted-imports)
property test: attempts == usage events; keys unique per attempt
quota store down -> paid call refused; bad BYOK key -> system-credit fallback visible and alerted
zip bomb / 10k-entry archive rejected before the first model call
cache hit ratio per call site from usage fields; prompt prefix diff across two users
metered sum vs provider usage export per provider per day within budget
same request sent twice within the TTL: the second call reads the stable prefix (cache-probe.mjs replay verdict ok); two tasks or users share the prefix up to the breakpoint
per call site from usage records: hit_pct over the hot-loop budget, reads per write over break-even, 1-hour writes metered as their own unit, gaps vs TTL
replay of real long turns through the compactor: prefix rewrites per 100 steps within budget, windows step on the same turns

every call site nobody waits on is listed with its trigger and is on a batch API, or has a written reason (a reply needed within minutes, chained steps); spend share within cost.batchable_sync_share_max
two consecutive calls of one conversation: tools, tool_choice, thinking and effort identical, and the serialized request up to the last breakpoint equal (cache-probe.mjs replay verdict ok)
a batch with a shared prefix: cache read share over its results (Anthropic reports 30-98% as best effort); prefix written first with a 1-hour TTL

tactics.tactic: One breakpoint on the last block that stays identical across requests; the timestamp and the incoming message go after it
tactics.when: a breakpoint on per-call content, or automatic caching on a unique last block
tactics.saving: reads at 0.1x instead of writes at 1.25x on the stable prefix

tactics.tactic: Move the date or time after the breakpoint (user turn or its own block), at day granularity unless the task needs more
tactics.when: the clock, an id or a place inside the system prompt or a marked block
tactics.saving: the system prompt and everything before the date stay cached

tactics.tactic: Use Message Batches for this job: one batch, custom_id per item, poll or webhook, handle errored and expired results
tactics.when: nobody waits for the result within minutes: nightly, cron, backfill, re-index, evals, bulk extraction
tactics.saving: -50% on input and output; most batches end within 1 h, at most 24 h; up to 100,000 requests or 256 MB per batch

tactics.tactic: Combine Batches with caching: identical cache_control blocks in every request, a 1-hour TTL, and the shared prefix written by one request before the rest are submitted
tactics.when: a batch whose requests share a long prefix (instructions, a document, examples)
tactics.saving: discounts stack (a cached read is ~0.05x base input in a batch); hits are best effort, 30-98% reported

tactics.tactic: Use the 1-hour TTL only where reuses land 5-60 min apart; keep 5 minutes for prefixes used more often than every 5 minutes (refreshed at no charge)
tactics.when: measured gaps between reuses of one prefix
tactics.saving: 1-hour (2 + 0.1k) beats 5-minute (1.25(k+1)) from one late reuse per hour; beats no cache above 1.11 reads per write

tactics.tactic: Send one call, wait for its first response, then fan out the rest that share the prefix
tactics.when: parallel calls (Promise.all, gather, a worker pool) over one shared prefix
tactics.saving: N-1 writes become reads (0.1x instead of 1.25x)

tactics.tactic: Keep tool_choice, disable_parallel_tool_use, thinking config and effort fixed for a conversation; when one must vary, place a breakpoint before the variation point
tactics.when: a request parameter chosen per call
tactics.saving: history stays cached across turns instead of being rewritten on each flip

tactics.tactic: Multi-turn: breakpoint on the last block of each request (automatic caching, or explicit on the last user turn); add a second breakpoint when a turn can add 20 or more blocks
tactics.when: a growing conversation or agent loop
tactics.saving: each turn reads the previous history and writes only the new turn

tactics.tactic: Clear tool results with hysteresis: trigger high, clear_at_least a large chunk, exclude_tools for results that must stay
tactics.when: context editing or a custom compactor in a loop
tactics.saving: one cache rewrite per clear instead of one per step

tactics.tactic: Breakpoint at the end of the system prompt, apart from the conversation, so compaction writes only the summary
tactics.when: server or client compaction of a long conversation
tactics.saving: the system prompt stays cached across each compaction

tactics.tactic: Keep thinking blocks (clear_thinking keep: "all") when cache hits matter more than context room; pass them back unchanged
tactics.when: thinking with tool use in long loops
tactics.saving: clearing thinking invalidates the cache at the clearing point

tactics.tactic: Count the prefix with the free count_tokens endpoint against the model's minimum cacheable length (512 to 4,096 tokens by model) before adding a breakpoint
tactics.when: a short system prompt or tool list marked for caching
tactics.saving: no silent no-op breakpoints; the endpoint is free (rate limited)

tactics.tactic: Keep synchronous calls (cached) where a person waits or steps chain; batch only the independent bulk part
tactics.when: a batch API on an interactive or multi-step flow
tactics.saving: minutes instead of up to 24 h per step
